_about: Single source of truth for every rendering, and the auditable term ledger (check 5). ONE rendering per referent for the whole book. Before you romanize any name, check here. status per entry: 'attested' (form used in English scholarship, give the citation in note), 'provisional' (your romanization, not found in outside sources), 'decided' (a project style call). If you find a better attested form mid-book, change it here AND grep every built chapter for the old form, then rebuild. Sections are top-level keys, rendered as glossary headings; keys starting with '_' are ignored. Rows nest UNDER a section: {section: {hanzi: {en, pinyin, status, note, ...}}}. apparatus_merge.py files each row under its 'category' field (default 'terms'). Add/rename sections freely (people, organizations, places, terms, ...).

林楠笙.cast: A Nationalist (Juntong) intelligence agent in occupied Shanghai; the novel's protagonist.
林楠笙.note: The protagonist; a Juntong agent. Pinyin.

朱怡贞.cast: A Communist intelligence agent and Lin Nansheng's first love; wife, in cover, of Ji Zhongyuan.
朱怡贞.note: A Communist agent; Lin's former student and lover. Endearment 贞贞, Zhenzhen. Pinyin.

顾慎言.cast: Lin Nansheng's superior and former training-class director; an elegant, cultivated spymaster.
顾慎言.note: Lin's superior and the director of studies of his training class. Pinyin.

左秋明.cast: A fellow trainee of Lin Nansheng's, now a Juntong liaison officer in Hong Kong.
左秋明.note: Lin's classmate from the training class; a liaison officer. Pinyin.

纪中原.cast: A Communist controller posing as a seal-engraver; Zhu Yizhen's husband in cover.
纪中原.note: Zhu Yizhen's controller and cover-husband; introduces himself as 'Old Ji.' Pinyin.

丁默邨.cast: A real turncoat: director of the No. 76 secret service of the Wang Jingwei regime.
丁默邨.note: Historical (1901–1947); Nationalist officer turned collaborator, co-founder of No. 76; executed as a traitor in 1947. Pinyin, the standard form in English scholarship.

铃木正男.note: The Japanese army surgeon who treats Lin in Hong Kong; addresses Lin as 'Pang-san.' Japanese reading.

小林大介.note: A second secretary at the Japanese consulate in Shanghai who trades intelligence with Lin. Japanese reading.

孟安南.note: An agent Gu Shenyan planted in Hong Kong years earlier; a member of the Indochinese Communist Party in cover. Pinyin.

童自重.note: A military-political adviser to the Wang regime; his Japanese army registry name is Uemura Kiyoshi (上村净). Assassinated at the Cathay Hotel. Pinyin.

蓝小姐.note: A celebrated Shanghai socialite (交际花) who serves as Lin's assistant in the assassination attempt. Pinyin of her surname.

老潘.note: The Communist contact who reactivates Zhu Yizhen after Ji Zhongyuan's presumed death. Pinyin.

汪精卫.note: Historical (1883–1944); leader of the Japanese-sponsored collaborationist government at Nanjing. Standard English form.

戴笠.note: Historical (1897–1946); head of the Juntong, the Nationalist military secret service. Called 'Mr. Dai' in the text. Standard English form.

胡主任.note: An officer of the Juntong headquarters inspectorate in Chongqing who sets Lin to watch Gu Shenyan. A fictional character; surname romanized.

潘新民.note: Old Pan's full name, given under interrogation; code name Index Finger. Pinyin.

荣将军.note: A general of the Nationalist Ministry of National Defense's Operations Department; a Communist agent, his home name Liu Zongming. Surname romanized.

刘宗铭.note: General Rong's name in his native place; he and Old Pan served together in the Nineteenth Route Army. Pinyin.

子璐.note: Miss Lan's son, killed in a stray-bullet crossfire. Pinyin of his given name.

黎广文.note: Meng Annan's cover name in postwar Shanghai, working as an editor at the French Photo Agency; Zhu Yizhen passes in cover as his wife, Mrs. Li. Pinyin.

阮志中.note: Meng Annan's true Vietnamese name; his parents, followers of Ho Chi Minh, died in a French prison in Saigon. Vietnamese form (Nguyễn Chí Trung).

胡志明.note: Historical (1890–1969); Vietnamese revolutionary, later president of North Vietnam. Standard English form.

徐德林.note: A postman at the Jing'an office and a Communist courier, tortured to death by the Japanese; Zhongliang's father. A fictional character; pinyin.

仲良.note: Xu Zhongliang (徐仲良), the postman's son and the story's protagonist. The given name pairs 仲 (“second-born”) with 良 (“good, upright”). A fictional character; pinyin.

徐嫂.note: Xu Delin's wife. 嫂 (sao), literally “elder brother's wife,” is a familiar address for a married woman of one's own generation, here roughly “Mrs. Xu”; the form is kept. A fictional character; pinyin.

周三.note: Doorman of the Jing'an post office and Zhongliang's Communist controller. 周三 means “Zhou Three,” a plain number-name of the sort given a laborer's son. A fictional character; pinyin.

苏丽娜.note: A Communist agent married in cover to an army officer, later a dance-hostess. The modern-sounding given name 丽娜 (“Lina”) suits her cosmopolitan cover. A fictional character; pinyin.

潘先生.note: The Communist handler over Zhou San and Su Lina in Shanghai. A fictional character; surname romanized. Distinct from Old Pan of The Rebel.

周楚康.note: Su Lina's husband, a lieutenant colonel of the National Revolutionary Army who returns to the front. A fictional character; pinyin.

秦兆宽.note: A collaborator with the Wang Jingwei regime, general manager of the Dahua Trading Company and a Japanese liaison; Su Lina's target. A fictional character; pinyin.

仲村信夫.note: A Japanese intelligence officer in Shanghai. A fictional character; Japanese reading of 仲村信夫.

秀芬.note: The widow of a killed guerrilla commissar, brought by Zhou San to keep house for Zhongliang. A fictional character; pinyin.

布朗神父.note: The English priest of St. Thérèse's Church. A fictional character; 布朗 is the source's transliteration of “Brown.”

俞鸿均.note: Yu Hongjun (俞鸿钧, 1898–1960; O.K. Yui), mayor of Shanghai at the time of the 1937 Japanese invasion. Historical. The source prints the name 俞鸿均; the attested figure is 俞鸿钧.

陈素农.note: Chen Sunong (1900–1983), a Whampoa graduate recorded as chief of staff of the 88th Division. A real officer.

黄庭坚.note: Huang Tingjian (1045–1105), Song-dynasty poet and one of the great masters of calligraphy. Historical.

克鲁格.note: Father Kruger (克鲁格), the fair-haired German priest who succeeds Father Brown as the church's intelligence contact and later strikes his own bargain with Zhongliang. A fictional character; the source's transliteration of a German surname (Kruger/Krüger).

伊藤近二.note: The Japanese agent, planted as a postal inspector at the Jing'an office, who has lived twenty years in Shanghai and been exiled to it for defeatist talk. A fictional character; Japanese name in Hepburn romanization.

陈泰泞.note: The bald, self-effacing warehouse clerk at Shiliupu whom Qin Zhaokuan charges, in secret, with getting Su Lina safely out of Shanghai. A fictional character; pinyin.

原田.note: Mr. Harada (原田先生), the aged proprietor of the Japanese pawnshop on Fourth Avenue who keeps Qin Zhaokuan's sealed box against the day the ring appears. A fictional character; Japanese surname.

潘汉年.note: Pan Hannian (1906–1977), the Communists’ chief intelligence officer in Shanghai and a Deputy Mayor of the city after 1949; purged in 1955, died in prison in 1977, rehabilitated 1982. Historical.

陈毅.note: Chen Yi (1901–1972), PLA marshal, first mayor of Shanghai after 1949 and later foreign minister. Historical.

罗瑞卿.note: Luo Ruiqing (1906–1978), a senior PLA general and the first Minister of Public Security of the People’s Republic. Historical.

杨复纲.note: Mr. Pan’s true name, revealed after his death; a martyr killed near Suqian in 1942. A fictional character; pinyin.

陈科长.note: The public-security section chief who interrogates and at last releases Su Lina and Zhongliang after 1949. A fictional character; surname romanized. Distinct from Chen Taining and from Chen Yi.

尤可常.note: The Chinese name taken by the former Japanese agent Itō Kinji after the war, when he stays on as the post office doorman. A fictional character; pinyin.

军统.note: The Nationalists' military Bureau of Investigation and Statistics, Dai Li's secret service, seated in Chongqing. Attested English abbreviation.

中统.note: The Nationalist party's (CC Clique's) Bureau of Investigation and Statistics, the Juntong's civilian rival. Attested English abbreviation.

特工总部.note: The Wang regime's secret-service headquarters at No. 76 Jessfield Road.

新四军.note: A Communist army operating in central-eastern China; nominally allied with the Nationalists against Japan. Standard English form.

和平建国军.note: The Wang regime's armed forces, in full the Peace National Construction Army.

中美合作所.note: SACO, the joint Nationalist–US intelligence and training body (1943) under Dai Li and Milton Miles. Attested English name.

蓝衣社.note: The Blue Shirts Society, a fascist-influenced Nationalist secret organization tied to the Juntong. Attested English name.

特高课.note: The Japanese Special Higher Police (特別高等警察), the political and thought police. Attested English/Japanese term.

中储银行.note: The note-issuing bank of the Wang Jingwei regime.

华兴洋行.note: A silk-and-tea export firm; the Juntong's Shanghai intelligence relay in cover.

良友.note: The famous illustrated pictorial of Republican Shanghai (1926–1945). Attested English title.

大公报.note: A major, respected Chinese newspaper. Attested romanization.

中华日报.note: The chief newspaper of the Wang Jingwei regime.

中央日报.note: The Nationalist party's official newspaper. Attested English name.

路透社.note: The British news agency; Lin's journalistic cover. Attested English name.

朵云轩.note: The famous Shanghai studio for painting, calligraphy, and seal-carving (founded 1900). Attested romanization.

沪江大学.note: A Baptist missionary university in Shanghai (Hujiang University). Attested English name.

保密局.note: The postwar reorganization of the Juntong. Romanized abbreviation, kept distinct from its wartime predecessor.

忠义救国军.note: Dai Li's guerrilla and paramilitary force. Attested English name.

力行社.note: The secret inner core of the Blue Shirts, tied to Dai Li. Attested romanization.

中央银行.note: The Nationalist government's central bank; not to be confused with the Wang regime's Central Reserve Bank. Attested English name.

华东局.note: The Chinese Communist Party's regional bureau for East China. Attested English name.

东方通讯社.note: A news agency Lin heads in cover in postwar Shanghai.

十九路军.note: The Nationalist army that defended Shanghai against Japan in 1932. Attested English name.

旅欧中国少年共产党.en: the Chinese Youth Communist Party in Europe
旅欧中国少年共产党.note: The European branch of the early Chinese Communist movement, founded in Paris in 1922. Attested English rendering.

三野.note: One of the People's Liberation Army's field armies in the civil war. Attested English name.

志愿军.note: The Chinese People's Volunteer Army sent to fight in the Korean War. Attested English name.

大华洋行.note: Qin Zhaokuan's front company. A fictional firm; 洋行 rendered “Trading Company.”

八十八师.note: A German-trained elite infantry division of the National Revolutionary Army, sent to the 1937 Battle of Shanghai. Historical.

松江支队.note: A Communist-led guerrilla unit near Shanghai; Xiufen's husband was its political commissar. Fictional or semi-historical within the story.

东京帝国大学.note: The pre-war name of the University of Tokyo. Historical.

汪伪政府.note: The Japanese-sponsored Reorganized National Government under Wang Jingwei (established Nanjing, 1940). Historical; 汪伪 = “Wang puppet.”

上海泰晤士报.note: An English-language daily of treaty-port Shanghai. Historical.

抗日除奸队.note: 抗日除奸队, a resistance cell of the kind that hunted collaborators and turncoats in occupied Shanghai; here the unit to which Xiufen belongs. Rendered descriptively.

264旅.note: The Nationalist brigade of the 88th Division in which Su Lina's husband, Zhou Chukang, serves at the front.

圣玛丽公学院.note: The elite Episcopal girls’ school in Shanghai (properly 圣玛利亚女校, St. Mary’s Hall, so named 1881); Su Lina’s school. The source’s 圣玛丽公学院 is a non-standard form. Historical.

招商局.note: The China Merchants Steam Navigation Company (轮船招商局, founded 1872), China’s first modern steamship line; its Huangpu warehouses are fought over in the taking of Shanghai. Historical.

反战同盟.note: The Japanese People’s Anti-war Alliance (日本人民反战同盟, formed 1939 under Kaji Wataru from Japanese prisoners of war); Itō claims membership to explain his survival. Historical.

四野.note: The Fourth Field Army (第四野战军) of the PLA, Lin Biao’s army grown out of the Northeast forces; so renamed in 1949. Historical.

极司菲尔路.note: A road in western Shanghai, today's Wanhangdu Road; No. 76 stood here. Attested period English name.

愚园路.note: A fashionable road in western Shanghai. Attested form (per the translation shelf).

巨籁达路.note: A French Concession street lined with plane trees, today's Julu Road. Attested French name.

霞飞路.note: The main thoroughfare of the French Concession, today's Central Huaihai Road. Attested French name.

苏州河.note: The river through central Shanghai. Attested English form.

众坊街.note: A street in Yau Ma Tei, Hong Kong. Attested official English name.

洛克道.note: A street in Wan Chai, Hong Kong. Attested official English name.

大屿山.note: The large island west of Hong Kong. Attested English form.

广州湾.note: A French-leased territory on the Guangdong coast, today's Zhanjiang. Attested romanization.

启德机场.note: Hong Kong's airport. Attested English name.

重庆.note: The Nationalist wartime capital. Attested pinyin form (per the shelf).

华懋饭店.note: Victor Sassoon's Cathay Hotel on the Bund; today the north building of the Peace Hotel. Attested English name.

歌乐山.note: The hills west of Chongqing where the Juntong and SACO kept training grounds and a prison. Attested romanization.

嘉陵江.note: The river that joins the Yangtze at Chongqing. Attested English form.

延安.note: The Communists' wartime capital in northern Shaanxi. Attested pinyin.

斜塘镇.note: A small water-country town on the outskirts of Shanghai where Lin hides as a schoolteacher. Pinyin.

静安寺.note: A famous ancient Buddhist temple in central Shanghai; the district and road bear its name. Attested English form.

爱丁堡大厦.note: An apartment building beside the Jing'an Temple; Lin's Shanghai residence. Rendered by the English place-name in the source.

兆丰公园.note: A western-Shanghai park, known in English as Jessfield Park, today's Zhongshan Park. Romanized from the Chinese name.

百乐门.note: The celebrated Art Deco dance hall of 1930s–40s Shanghai. Attested English name (百乐门 transliterates 'Paramount').

丹桂戏园.note: A long-established Shanghai opera house. Attested romanization.

西柏坡.note: The Hebei village that served as the Communist central headquarters in 1948. Attested pinyin.

富阳.note: A district of Hangzhou, Zhejiang; Lin's claimed native place under his alias. Attested pinyin.

督邮街.note: The busiest night district of wartime Chongqing. Pinyin.

金都大戏院.note: A cinema on Avenue Foch in Shanghai; the site of the military-police gunfight. Rendered by the theater's period English name.

福熙路.note: A French Concession boulevard, today's central Yan'an Middle Road. Attested French name.

圣类思中学.note: A Catholic mission school in Xietang where Lin teaches (类思 renders the Christian name Aloysius).

南宁.note: The capital of Guangxi, in the region where Ho Chi Minh was jailed by the Nationalists. Attested pinyin.

静安邮政所.note: The neighborhood post office where Xu Delin and Zhongliang serve. Fictional workplace; named for the Jing'an district.

小德肋撒堂.note: A real Catholic church dedicated to St. Thérèse of Lisieux. 德肋撒 is the Catholic transliteration of Thérèse/Teresa. Historical.

万国殡仪馆.note: The best-known funeral home of Republican Shanghai (opened 1926). Historical.

四明公寓.note: A 1932 lane compound in the French Concession, built as staff housing for the Siming Bank (四明邨/四明公寓). Historical.

虹口.note: The Shanghai district north of Suzhou Creek, center of the Japanese settlement and its military and intelligence presence. Historical.

四马路.note: Sima Road (today Fuzhou Road), the Republican-era street of brothels, teahouses, and publishers; the calque “Fourth Avenue” follows 四马路 (“fourth horse road”).

松江.note: A county town southwest of Shanghai. Historical.

东亚旅馆.note: A Shanghai hotel named in the story. Rendered by sense.

泰顺茶庄.note: A tea shop used as a courier channel. A fictional front; pinyin.

海关钟楼.note: The tower of the Maritime Customs House on the Bund, its Westminster-chiming clock (“Big Ching”) completed 1927. Historical.

长沙.note: The capital of Hunan, site of the Battles of Changsha (1939–1944) in the war against Japan. Historical.

南京.note: The Nationalist capital until 1937; later seat of the Wang Jingwei regime. Historical.

武汉.note: The tri-city on the middle Yangtze, provisional Nationalist center after the fall of Nanjing. Historical.

西摩路.note: A road in the western International Settlement, today Shaanxi North Road (陕西北路). Zhongliang keeps his cigarette stall at a corner off it.

桥楼.note: Bridge House (桥楼), by the Sichuan Road bridge over Suzhou Creek: the Shanghai headquarters and torture-prison of the Kempeitai. Historical.

鹿儿岛.note: City and bay at the southern tip of Kyushu, Japan, where the navy rehearsed the Pearl Harbor attack. Attested.

名古屋.note: City in central Japan; the exiled inspector Itō Kinji's home town. Attested.

虹口公园.note: The park in the Hongkou district (今鲁迅公园), in the Japanese quarter of Shanghai; Zhongliang's last safe-house stands near it.

十六铺.note: The old wharf district on the Huangpu in southern Shanghai (the source also prints the variant 十六浦). Site of the Longxin Warehouse where Chen Taining works.

提篮桥.note: Tilanqiao Prison (built 1901–03), known in English as Ward Road Gaol; after 1945 it held collaborators and Japanese war criminals. Historical.

外白渡桥.note: The steel bridge (opened 1908) over Suzhou Creek at the Bund, known in English as the Garden Bridge. Historical.

交际花.note: Literally 'a flower of society'; a fashionable woman of the demimonde who moves among wealthy men.

旗袍.note: The close-fitting Chinese woman's dress; 'cheongsam' is the established English form.

黄包车.note: The man-pulled two-wheeled cab of Republican Shanghai.

皖南事变.note: The Southern Anhui Incident of January 1941. Attested English name.

淞沪会战.note: The battle of August–November 1937. Attested English name.

整风运动.note: The Communist ideological campaign begun at Yan'an in 1942. Attested English name.

蝶恋花.note: An embroidery motif of butterflies among blossoms; also a classical song-lyric tune title.

咏梅.note: The title of the poem used as a contact signal; a 七律 (regulated verse).

忘忧清乐集.note: A Song-dynasty classic of go; here it doubles as the key text of a cipher. Attested romanization.

汉奸.note: Literally a traitor to the Han, i.e. a collaborator with the Japanese; the postwar treason trials pursued them. Rendered 'traitor / collaborator' by context.

食指.note: Old Pan's code name; literally the index finger (the 'eating finger'). Rendered by sense.

布谷鸟在歌唱.note: A recognition signal Su Lina passes up the line. The story's own tradecraft.

舞林皇后.note: “Queen of the Dance World,” the title given the top dance-hostess, often by charity ballot.

人丹.note: Small refreshing medicinal pellets; 人丹 is the Chinese brand answering the Japanese Jintan (仁丹).

鲶鱼.note: Zhongliang's code name after he takes over Zhou San's work (鲶鱼, “catfish”); he plays on it in English with Father Kruger.

储备券.note: 储备券, the banknotes of the Wang regime's Central Reserve Bank; the currency of occupied Shanghai.

三炮台.note: 三炮台, the Chinese name for the Wills brand Three Castles, a premium foreign cigarette of Republican Shanghai.

青天白日满地红.en: the Blue Sky, White Sun, and Wholly Red Earth flag
青天白日满地红.note: The national flag of the Republic of China, flown also by Wang Jingwei's collaborationist regime.

清乡.note: 清乡 (qingxiang), the Japanese and Wang-regime campaign to pacify and control the countryside around occupied Shanghai.

石库门.note: 石库门, the stone-framed-gate lane-house characteristic of Shanghai.

榻榻米.note: 榻榻米, the Japanese straw-mat flooring, fitting the safe-house in the Japanese residents' quarter.

士林布.note: Cotton dyed with Indanthren, the German synthetic vat-dye prized for not fading; ubiquitous in 1930s–40s China. Historical.
